comparator.name: Communication and Information Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: This example follows the curriculum for September 2026 entrants. It includes Humane AI and Digital Society as the first-year elective, its second-year project course and a 30 EC minor. The regular pathway is taught in English, including the thesis. Groningen also offers a Dutch track.
components: Studies how media and physical forms shape communication.
Studies how persuasion and arguments influence attitudes.
Builds academic skills for studying communication.
Observing Communication in the Wild: Qualitative Methods
Develops qualitative research skills for studying communication.
Studies how readers process and interpret texts.
Studies how people use language in interaction.
Humane AI in Digital Societies: Introduction
One of the two first-year faculty-wide choices.
Studies communication in organizations and workplaces.
Develops quantitative approaches to communication research.
Studies discourse and how platform features shape interaction.
Develops statistical analysis for communication research.
Studies language in its context of use.
Humane AI in Digital Societies: Projects
One of four faculty-wide choices. This example continues the first-year Humane AI theme.
Studies communication in relation to social change.
Studies literacy practices and their place in society.

A supervised research seminar and thesis, normally written in English on this pathway.
Applies communication study to an integrated case.

routeSelection.basis: The unqualified degree target follows the regular English-taught pathway. The Dutch track has specified Dutch-language seminars, assessments and thesis. The 2026 entry regulations list two first-year electives. This example uses the first listed, Humane AI and Digital Society. The second-year project course continues that theme from among the four faculty-wide choices.

alternatives.label: Communication, discourse and media
alternatives.labelReason: The title describes the main methods and settings studied in the plan.
alternatives.concept: Study how rhetoric, language and visual media shape public meaning. Analyze arguments, film and environmental narratives, practice public speaking, and use qualitative and quantitative methods to investigate communication.
progression: Foundations in rhetoric, media and sociology lead into community speaking, stylistics and media analysis. Research methods and comparative interpretation support advanced persuasion, documentary work and historical research.

alternatives.label: Workplace and health communication
alternatives.labelReason: The title describes the main methods and settings studied in the plan.
alternatives.concept: Study how people communicate across cultural and professional settings. Explore negotiation, inclusive leadership and persuasion, and examine how communication shapes decisions in health care.
progression: Foundations in rhetoric, psychology and research precede negotiation, organizational psychology, health psychology and advanced research synthesis. The introductory brain and behavior course precedes the first available psycholinguistics course.
alternatives.distinctness: 12 courses and 90 EC differ in each direction from option 1. The distinct focus is workplace interaction, health behavior and consultation, and leadership in diverse settings.

alternatives.label: Digital media and AI communication
alternatives.labelReason: The title describes the main methods and settings studied in the plan.
alternatives.concept: Study how digital platforms and AI shape communication. Analyze social and documentary media, use data and language models to investigate digital material, and examine how organizations make responsible decisions about technology.
progression: Programming, data science, mathematics, rhetoric and film provide foundations for machine learning, media research and digital strategy. AI ethics and decision methods precede advanced work with neural networks, text classification and generation.
alternatives.distinctness: 12 courses and 90 EC differ in each direction from option 1. 13 courses and 97.5 EC differ in each direction from option 2. The distinct focus is platform media, digital strategy, AI ethics, data and language models.

blocks: Both study how arguments and persuasive choices shape a message. UCR focuses on rhetoric, public speaking and written argument.
Both examine how language works in interaction. UCR studies turn-taking and dialogue within a broader course on stylistics.
Both address cognitive aspects of language. UCR studies reading and comprehension alongside spoken language and language disorders.
Both study how the material form of a medium shapes communication. UCR traces the technologies and artifacts of media history.
Groningen studies social-media discourse and platform features. UCR examines storytelling and representation across older and newer media.
Groningen studies communication and societal change. UCR courses explore specific examples such as climate communication and racial representation.
Both examine communication in organizations. UCR focuses on leadership, storytelling and persuasion.
Both examine communication in health care. UCR studies consultation and shared decisions within a wider health psychology course.
Groningen has a dedicated intercultural communication course. UCR studies culture and identity across sociology, rhetoric and leadership.
Groningen studies language in context. UCR approaches context through stylistics and social theory.
Both develop academic skills. UCR includes source evaluation, research questions and academic writing.
Both use qualitative research to investigate social meaning. UCR covers interviews, observation and interpretation across a range of social questions.
Both develop statistical analysis. UCR combines statistics with experimental methods and examples from psychology.
Groningen applies quantitative methods specifically to communication. UCR applies these methods in psychology and market research.
Groningen has a dedicated design and evaluation course for communication. UCR offers broader study in research design and measurement.
Digital communication, data and responsible AI
Groningen’s faculty elective links AI with digital society. UCR explores AI ethics and technical AI methods in separate courses.
Groningen continues its faculty-wide AI theme through a project course. UCR offers separate work in AI ethics, media and data.
Groningen reserves 30 EC for an approved minor.
Groningen studies literacy as a social practice in a dedicated course.
Groningen requires a 10 EC thesis and research seminar. UCR’s optional research element sits outside its degree schedule.
Groningen has a dedicated 10 EC communication case study.

selection.assessment: Three complete plans meet course feasibility and distinctness. Their separate emphases are communication and media analysis, workplace and health settings, and digitally mediated communication and AI.

core: Human communication through language, images, interaction and context
Media narratives, visual communication and digital platforms
Corporate, intercultural, health and societal communication
Qualitative and quantitative research, intervention design and evaluation
adjacent: Digital, social-media, human-computer and AI communication
questions: How do language, images and interaction create meaning across contexts?
How do persuasion, narratives and platforms shape attitudes and public life?
How can communication interventions be designed and evaluated responsibly?

notes.text: The UCR options share methods and topics with Groningen. Groningen combines dedicated courses in language and interaction, communication research, design and evaluation, and a required communication thesis.
This curriculum applies to students starting at Groningen in September 2026.

audience.programmeDescription: Study how people use language, images and media to make meaning and influence others. The regular Groningen pathway is taught in English. A Dutch track is also available.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Groningen combines communication analysis, practical applications and research. The UCR options emphasize discourse and media, workplace and health communication, or digital media and AI.
